text: By , and Listen (2 min) Protesters opposed to Oracle’s ‘Project Jupiter’ data center gathered in Santa Fe, N.M., in August. Susan Montoya Bryan / Associated Press Oracle set out last year to lease a massive AI data-center campus being built in New Mexico ’s Doña Ana County, part of a blitz of deals to create computing power for OpenAI. The company made aggressive financial commitments for the facility in contracts that allow it little wiggle room. Now, “Project Jupiter” is mired in challenges over power supply and permitting and is fast becoming a prime example of the risks in the tech giant’s sprawling and expensive artificial-intelligence gambit.
